summary: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche works in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Geshe degree at the Dialectic School of Menri and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, later serving as its president, and was a Rockefeller Fellow at Rice University (1991).

Ter Ellingson is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, he served as a music professor at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

Terese Tse Bartholomew is a specialist in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Sinology. She earned an M.A. from the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum (attested 1985–2003).
Terry Kleeman is a scholar in Sinology and religious studies who studied at the University of British Columbia. He has served as a professor at the University of Colorado Boulder since circa 1998.
Tertön Sogyal studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tohoku University, serving as president (1963–1966), and later served as president of Miyagi University of Education and professor at Keio and Komazawa universities.

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Florida State University and the University of Virginia (PhD). She taught at the University of Virginia, Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis, and Florida State University.
Tessa Verney Wheeler was a scholar in history and archaeology. She was educated at Addey and Stanhope School from 1905 to 1911 and at University College London from 1911 to 1914.

Tetsuei Sato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later served as a professor at Taisho University, Gifu Kyoritsu University (circa 1972), and as an emeritus professor at Ryukoku University (circa 1970–1982).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue was a philosophy and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as professor and dean at the University of Tokyo and as president of Daito Bunka University.

Tetsuo Otani is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He held multiple leadership roles, including president of Komazawa University (2002–2006), chairman of Tsuru University (2013–2016), and president of Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019).

Tetsuro Noguchi was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at Yokohama National University (circa 1967–1974), the University of Tsukuba (circa 1974–1996), and J. F. Oberlin University (circa 1996–2003).

Tetsuro Watsuji was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University, and held professorial chairs in ethics at Kyoto University (1925–1949) and the University of Tokyo (1934–1949).

Tetsuzo Tanikawa was a scholar of philosophy and Japanology. He completed his studies at Kyoto University's Faculty of Letters (1919–1922) and held academic posts at Doshisha University (circa 1928–1933) and Hosei University (circa 1938–1968).
Teun Goudriaan is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held positions at Utrecht University, where he is attested as a committee member in 1989 and as Professor Emeritus in 2000.
Thanissaro Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Oberlin College and trained under Ajahn Fuang Jotiko. He founded Metta Forest Monastery, serving as its abbot beginning in 1993.
Thanon Chitkament is a researcher in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under the guidance of Vishwas D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi (attested 2021).

Theodoor Paul Galestin was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied under Nicolaas Johannes Krom. In 1957, he was appointed professor of South and Southeast Asian archaeology and ancient history at Leiden University.

Theodor Aufrecht was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at the Bodleian Library and served as a professor at the University of Edinburgh (1861–1875) and the University of Bonn (1875–1889).
